title: REST Assured: API testing in Java with a fluent syntax

videos.script: Lessons 4 to 6 kept your tests in a collection, a JSON file that a tool runs. This lesson writes them in Java, with a library called REST Assured. {{java}} Many teams build their server in Java. They often test its API in Java too, in the same repository, run by the same build. {{repo}} First you install a Java Development Kit and Maven. Maven is the build tool that downloads REST Assured and runs your tests. {{install}} Then you write tests that read almost like a sentence. Given this request, when it is sent, then the answer looks like this. {{gwt}} You take a token out of one answer and send it with the next request, the way a real client does. {{chain}} You move what every test repeats into one place, so the address of the server is written once. {{spec}} And you meet a build that says success after running no tests at all. It is a real trap, and the fix is a few lines in one file. {{zero}} By the end, the defect from lesson 1 fails a Java test, with the request and the response printed beside it.
